evals.name: atomic-review-uses-semantic-role-slices-without-hiding-unselected-evidence
evals.prompt: A Word template yields 186 atomic decision groups, including nine page-frame and nine column-flow source units that may be grouped by identical evidence. The next model must reconstruct the one-column-to-two-column transition before reviewing captions or body runs. State how to create its bounded work packet and what remains true about the other groups.
evals.expected_output: Generate the review queue with --roles page.frame,page.columns and then --batch-size 20 --batch-index 1 plus a batch-template output. This produces a stable page-geometry slice while retaining the full ledger count and pending status for all nonselected groups. Identical page units may appear as fewer grouped review decisions. The filtered queue is a work-order aid, not an audit exemption or a fidelity claim.
expectations: --roles accepts a comma-separated set of source-backed role names and applies batching after the semantic selection.
The review report records both matching groups and the full decision-group count.
The evidence-bound batch draft contains only selected pending group keys and still requires final dispositions before merge.
Unselected evidence stays in the immutable ledger, remains pending, and continues to block strict completion and PDF calibration.

evals.name: front-matter-metadata-remains-an-editable-interface-instead-of-title-author-filler
evals.prompt: An IEEE-style Word template contains a publication-date line, DOI label, received date, and correspondence notice before the abstract. The initial generated package has title, author, affiliation, and date fields but no explicit metadata interface. Explain the required reconstruction and review behavior.
evals.expected_output: Classify these units as front_matter.metadata, not title or author text. Review them as a metadata slice and create or use the class-level journalmetadata interface with editable main.tex content. Keep each source-backed layout decision auditable; missing evidence remains a gap rather than being hidden in a generic author block.
expectations: Publication and editorial metadata stays distinct from title, author, and affiliation decisions.
The generated class exposes an editable \journalmetadata interface and the default main.tex invokes it without forcing non-source text to render.
The review queue provides metadata-specific ownership hints and asks the model to add the interface when an older package lacks it.
A metadata slice does not permit a full-fidelity or PDF-calibration claim while unrelated source evidence remains pending.

evals.name: headless-miktex-missing-package-is-a-fast-environment-diagnosis-not-a-template-failure
evals.prompt: A generated package is compiled in a headless Windows environment using MiKTeX. The required titlesec.sty package is absent and MiKTeX would normally wait for an installer prompt. State the expected compile behavior and handoff classification.
evals.expected_output: The compiler disables MiKTeX auto-install by default, returns quickly, and writes a compile report with diagnostics.failure_category set to missing_tex_dependency and titlesec.sty in missing_tex_dependencies. The conversion package remains usable, but compile and PDF comparison are pending local verification; the agent must not call the missing dependency a reconstruction defect. Automatic installation is opt-in via --allow-auto-install.
expectations: MiKTeX direct-engine commands include --disable-installer unless --allow-auto-install is explicitly supplied.
The report distinguishes missing_tex_dependency, timeout, engine-not-found, and LaTeX syntax failures.
The missing package filename is retained in machine-readable diagnostics.
No partial PDF enters a visual-comparison result, and no environment failure is reported as successful compilation.

evals.name: readiness-handoff-recommends-the-next-semantic-mapping-slice-from-pending-word-evidence
evals.prompt: A converted package has a complete Word ledger and 889 pending atomic units. The pending source-backed units include title, author, affiliation, DOI metadata, abstract, keywords, page geometry, tables, figures, and references. A second model must continue without re-reading the entire queue. State the required readiness handoff.
evals.expected_output: The readiness report stays in atomic_mapping and provides recommended_mapping_slice for front_matter, including the observed title/author/affiliation/metadata/abstract/keyword roles, role counts, and a package-directory --roles command hint. It remains a continuation checkpoint: all unselected units stay pending and PDF calibration remains blocked.
expectations: The recommendation is derived only from audit units still marked needs_decision and their source-backed candidate roles.
The earliest dependency-ordered semantic concern is chosen before later page, table, figure, or back-matter roles.
The command hint runs from the generated package directory, uses --package ., and supplies the exact --roles set.
The handoff explicitly retains the strict audit gate and does not represent a role-slice recommendation as completed conversion.

evals.name: word-list-system-is-a-separate-audited-layout-contract
evals.prompt: An official Word template contains a bulleted methods list and a two-level decimal list. numbering.xml defines different label text, start values, left indents, and hanging indents. Explain the required evidence extraction, mapping, and verification behavior.
evals.expected_output: Keep every visible list paragraph as body.list_item and create a separate body.list_system unit for each Word numbering definition. Map the system to editable journalitemize/journalenumerate behavior in journal-template.cls, map items to the source-backed list interface, and retain label geometry, nested levels, and restart behavior for same-content rendered confirmation. Do not treat list numbers as headings or accept a generic itemize environment as proof of fidelity.
expectations: The evidence record preserves numId or style fallback, level definitions, number format, level text, start value, and left/hanging indentation.
Reference-zone lists remain reference evidence rather than being mislabeled as ordinary body lists.
The review queue orders the list-system decision before list-item and ordinary body decisions and supplies class/main ownership hints.
Pending list evidence blocks a full-fidelity claim even if a generated PDF displays bullets or numbered items.

evals.name: omml-equations-have-separate-system-and-instance-audits
evals.prompt: A Word template has two centered OMML display equations with visible tags (1) and (2). One formula contains a literal caret in m:t rather than a semantic m:sSup element. State the required reconstruction and audit behavior.
evals.expected_output: Create equation.system evidence for display policy, counter/tag pattern, number placement, paragraph alignment, and appendix interaction; create one equation.instance record per OMML formula. Map the system to the editable journalequation class environment and each formula to equations.tex or an explicit manual-translation record. The literal caret must be marked ambiguous_raw_caret and remain manual translation rather than being fabricated as a superscript. A compiling generic amsmath equation does not prove source layout fidelity.
expectations: Equation objects preserve display versus inline context, visible number samples, paragraph index/alignment, conversion status, and unsupported structure.
The strict queue orders equation.system before equation.instance and requires editable class/equations.tex ownership hints.
A raw caret without m:sSup or m:sSubSup is retained as an explicit manual-translation gap, not translated into plausible exponent syntax.
Unresolved equation evidence blocks a full-fidelity and PDF-calibration claim even if the generic fixture compiles.

evals.name: word-paragraph-borders-and-shading-require-a-separate-block-decoration-owner
evals.prompt: A Word author template uses a shaded, four-sided framed abstract notice and a title style with an inherited bottom border. The generated LaTeX package has no source-specific block environment. State the required handling.
evals.expected_output: Capture borders, shading, frame/anchor settings, keep-lines and surrounding paragraph context in direct/effective Word formatting. Create one block.decoration unit for each decorated paragraph, including inherited style decoration. Record page.block_decorations in the spec and leave a source-specific LaTeX block interface as a required mapping gap until the model designs it and verifies it by rendering. Do not use an arbitrary colored box or call it matched merely because the ordinary package compiles.
expectations: Paragraph direct/effective formatting preserves each border side's style, width, spacing and color, plus shading, frame and pagination controls where present.
A styled title border and a directly formatted body/abstract block both create independent block.decoration evidence rather than being silently inherited by generic body styling.
The review queue requires a source-specific class/main block interface and keeps the item pending when that interface does not exist.
The rendered check compares block geometry and decoration, not merely text or compile success.

evals.name: word-section-page-numbering-is-not-inferred-from-page-field-placement
evals.prompt: A Word template has a front-matter section with w:pgNumType lowerRoman start=1 and a next-page body section with decimal start=1. Both footer variants contain PAGE fields. Explain the required reconstruction behavior.
evals.expected_output: Extract a page.numbering system with both section overrides, retain their Word boundaries and fields separately, and expose journalpagenumbering plus commented page-numbering.tex candidates for roman 1 and arabic 1. Do not auto-input either candidate or use a PAGE field to infer a global format. The model must confirm the semantic transition and rendered sequence before enabling the restart behavior.
expectations: The specification preserves format, start value, section index, chapter style and separator for each explicit pgNumType override.
The review queue treats page.numbering as a source-backed system before ordinary body work and demands a section-boundary decision.
Generated candidates map lowerRoman and decimal to LaTeX roman and arabic, but remain commented until a visual comparison validates the transition.
A dynamic PAGE field alone cannot satisfy page-numbering format or restart evidence.

evals.name: word-toc-entry-tabs-and-leaders-are-a-separate-layout-contract
evals.prompt: An official Word template contains a TOC field and TOC1 entries with a right-aligned tab at 9000 twips and dot leaders before the page number. The generated LaTeX package currently uses only \tableofcontents. State the required reconstruction behavior.
evals.expected_output: Extract the TOC field separately from entry layout evidence, including each TOC style or style ID, indentation, right-tab position, leader pattern, and page-number alignment. Create toc.structure for enabling the TOC and toc.layout for its source-specific geometry. Preserve the tab evidence in template_spec.json and leave toc.layout as a required editable class/main mapping until a source-specific interface is implemented and render-verified. Do not claim a standard LaTeX dotted TOC matches Word merely because it compiles.
expectations: TOC structure and TOC entry geometry are represented by different source-backed evidence units.
Entry evidence retains the Word style or style ID, indentation where present, tab position, alignment and leader pattern.
The strict review queue puts toc.layout ahead of generic body work and identifies journal-template.cls plus main.tex as the editable owners.
A compiling default \tableofcontents is insufficient proof of TOC layout fidelity and must not clear the source-specific layout audit.

evals.name: word-line-numbering-is-a-section-level-audited-system
evals.prompt: An official Word template has w:lnNumType countBy=5, start=1, distance=360, restart=newPage in its first section, and no line-numbering override in the second section. The generated package currently contains only \linenumbers. State the required reconstruction behavior.
evals.expected_output: Create a source-backed line.numbering system that retains the first section boundary, countBy interval, start number, distance in twips, restart policy, and paragraph-level suppress-line-number evidence when present. Provide an editable journallinenumbering interface and a commented line-numbering.tex candidate that maps 360 twips to 18pt, every fifth line, and pagewise behavior. Do not treat a global linenumbers call as proof that the source section policy is matched; retain the multi-section boundary as a render-verification requirement.
expectations: The system records Word countBy, start, distance, restart, and section boundary rather than only a boolean line-number flag.
The output exposes a class-owned line-numbering interface and source-labeled, commented section candidates.
The strict review queue treats line.numbering as an early page-system decision and does not let a global default silently satisfy it.
Rendered verification checks line-number interval, text-side distance, and restart behavior without using ordinary body text as a substitute.

evals.name: visible-non-toc-word-tabs-require-role-specific-layout-mapping
evals.prompt: An official Word template has a correspondence metadata paragraph containing a visible tab character. Its effective paragraph format has a right tab at 9000 twips with no leader. The document also contains a TOC with dot leaders. Explain the required reconstruction behavior.
evals.expected_output: Record the correspondence paragraph as paragraph.tab_stops with its paragraph index, semantic context, effective tab type and position, and any direct override. Keep it separate from toc.layout, write tab-stops.tex as source evidence, and require a role-specific class/main mapping before clearing the audit. Do not apply the TOC's dotted leader or a document-wide tab policy to correspondence metadata. Verify the label/value alignment in a rendered same-content page.
expectations: Only a visible tab character together with an effective tab-stop definition creates this system evidence; unused style tabs are not promoted.
TOC and non-TOC tab layouts remain independent roles with different owners and verification requirements.
The generated evidence file is not auto-input and no global tab default is claimed as a match.
The review queue requires a semantic role decision before LaTeX implementation and preserves right/left/center/decimal type, position, and leader where observed.

evals.name: partial-word-line-numbering-properties-remain-a-critical-gap
evals.prompt: A real Word template has w:lnNumType countBy=1 and restart=continuous, but omits start and distance. The generated package has journallinenumbering and a commented line-numbering.tex file. How must the skill report and handle this?
evals.expected_output: Preserve the observed countBy and restart values. Retain raw start omission while recording the documented OOXML default that restarts at 1; name the automatic/unspecified distance as a remaining gap in template_spec.json and format_gap_log.md, and leave the line-numbering candidate manual. The line.numbering role and the line-numbers feature remain needs_mapping until distance is confirmed by authoritative source or rendering. The existence of a macro, a commented candidate, or a compiling PDF cannot upgrade this partial evidence to mapped.
expectations: A documented OOXML default is recorded separately from the raw missing attribute; no LaTeX point value is invented for automatic distance.
The gap log names the remaining unresolved parameter and points to the editable candidate location.
Coverage uses needs_mapping for both the source feature and source-backed role while values remain absent.
A fixture with all explicit parameters can remain mapped_pending_visual_confirmation, demonstrating that completeness and visual verification are separate gates.

evals.name: word-drop-cap-is-a-combined-initial-and-body-layout-unit
evals.prompt: An official Word template has a paragraph containing only T with framePr dropCap=drop and lines=2, followed by a paragraph beginning HIS document is a template. Explain the required reconstruction behavior.
evals.expected_output: Create paragraph.drop_cap evidence containing the Word dropCap mode, line count, frame anchor/wrap attributes, the visible T, and the following HIS document paragraph. Generate a commented drop-caps.tex candidate using journaldropcap, but do not insert it automatically into generic manuscript text. Keep ordinary framePr paragraphs separate. The role remains pending visual confirmation until a same-content render verifies the initial height, text wrap, and paragraph boundary.
expectations: Only framePr with a dropCap value becomes drop-cap evidence; generic frame evidence remains separate.
The source records mode, line count, anchor/wrap properties, initial text, and following paragraph context.
The generated LaTeX package exposes a class-owned journaldropcap interface and a commented candidate rather than modifying unrelated body text.
Compile success alone cannot prove drop-cap geometry, wrapping, or baseline alignment.

evals.name: word-run-character-effects-remain-local-and-audited
evals.prompt: An official Word template uses small caps for a running label, yellow highlight for an editorial instruction, 90 percent character scale in a table header, and a raised baseline in a correspondence marker. Explain the required reconstruction behavior.
evals.expected_output: Capture each visible run span with its exact OOXML effect values and semantic context as run.character_effects. Write character-effects.tex as source evidence and keep the role needing a source-specific class/main mapping; do not apply a global textsc, highlight, scale, or raise rule. Preserve an editorial instruction as guidance rather than manuscript text, and confirm visible effects with a same-content render before claiming fidelity.
expectations: The evidence preserves small/all caps, highlight, hidden state, spacing, scale, baseline position, and text-effect flags when present.
Effects are represented as local run spans with paragraph and table-cell context, not as a global class typography decision.
The generated candidate records source values but does not auto-input or claim an arbitrary visual approximation as matched.
A plain-text compile does not clear the character-effects audit.

evals.name: unmodeled-ooxml-format-properties-must-be-classified-before-fidelity-claim
evals.prompt: A Word template scan records run properties kern, lang, bCs, and textFill plus paragraph properties adjustRightInd and autoSpaceDE. The current direct-format extractor has no dedicated fields for them. Explain the required reconstruction behavior.
evals.expected_output: Preserve the aggregated evidence in unmodeled-word-properties.json and expose it as word.unmodeled_format. Before a fidelity claim, classify each property as a visible role effect requiring source-specific LaTeX, a documented Word default, non-format metadata, or an explicit unresolved gap. Keep source part, occurrence count, and sample attributes. Do not silently discard it, infer a document-wide style, or clear the audit merely because the package compiles.
expectations: The generic inventory prevents silent property loss without claiming every OOXML node is visible typography.
Classification distinguishes source-backed visual effects, documented defaults, non-format metadata, and unresolved gaps.
A high-frequency unsupported property remains reviewable and blocks a full-fidelity claim until it has an explicit disposition.
The model does not install arbitrary global LaTeX settings or treat compile success as evidence of a correct classification.

evals.name: run-shading-and-kerning-threshold-are-local-character-evidence
evals.prompt: A Word template has a gray-shaded editorial marker and a colored inline label with w:shd on their runs. Its title style also has w:kern=28. Explain the required reconstruction behavior.
evals.expected_output: Record visible run shading attributes and the Word kerning threshold in run.character_effects with exact span and role context. If w:kern appears only in a named style, preserve it as named_style_rule evidence with the style identity rather than dropping it or calling it visually confirmed. Write both to character-effects.tex, keep them out of a document-wide default, and require a source-specific class/main mapping plus same-content rendering before a fidelity claim. Treat w:kern as a font-kerning threshold rather than a literal LaTeX kern length. Do not promote white/auto clear shading or w:kern=0 as visible effects.
expectations: Run shading and positive kerning thresholds are retained as local visible evidence or explicitly labelled named-style evidence with role context.
Default clear/auto/white shading and a zero kerning threshold do not create false visual-effect samples.
The package candidate records source facts without automatically applying an arbitrary global colorbox, tracking, or kern setting.
A successful compile does not prove that local shading or font kerning matches the Word renderer.

evals.name: word-rstyle-must-resolve-before-run-format-is-mapped
evals.prompt: A Word run contains ABSTRACT with no direct bold or colour properties, but its rPr has w:rStyle=H5CharChar. The named character style defines Helvetica, bold, and blue text. Explain the required reconstruction behavior.
evals.expected_output: Resolve H5CharChar before interpreting the run, then record run.character_styles with the character-style ID, resolved effective font formatting, local span boundary, source part, and semantic role context. Write character-styles.tex as evidence and require a role-specific class/main mapping plus same-content rendering. Do not treat the run as plain text, collapse it into the paragraph style, create a document-wide Helvetica/blue rule, or call the named style render-confirmed merely because it resolves in XML.
expectations: The effective run format includes the referenced character style before local direct formatting is applied.
Evidence retains the style identity, resolved status, source context, and local text span.
The generated candidate is evidence only and the strict audit remains needs_mapping until source-specific ownership is implemented.
Missing character-style definitions remain explicit unresolved evidence rather than being silently replaced with paragraph defaults.

evals.name: run-border-requires-visible-value-and-local-role-mapping
evals.prompt: A Word template has one run with w:bdr val=single, sz=8, space=2, color=00629B and several other runs with w:bdr val=none, sz=0. Explain the required reconstruction behavior.
evals.expected_output: Record only the active single border as run.character_effects with the exact border attributes, local span, and semantic context. Preserve it in character-effects.tex and require a source-specific local LaTeX mapping plus rendered verification. Recognize none/nil or zero-width borders as nonvisible XML defaults rather than generating false boxes. Do not apply a global fbox or generic colored border to the document.
expectations: The extractor preserves active run-border attributes but filters none/nil and zero-width placeholders from visible-effect evidence.
Run borders remain local source-role evidence, not a document-wide LaTeX frame decision.
The candidate remains non-auto-input and compile success does not clear its visual mapping audit.

evals.name: word-docgrid-and-snap-to-grid-require-cjk-specific-audit
evals.prompt: A bilingual Word template has section docGrid type=lines and linePitch=312. Its abstract style has snapToGrid=0 and autoSpaceDE=0, while body text inherits the section grid. Explain the required reconstruction behavior.
evals.expected_output: Record page.text_grid with the section docGrid and the abstract style's direct local overrides, and write text-grid.tex as source evidence. Keep grid policy separate from ordinary paragraph line spacing. Do not automatically enable a global LaTeX baseline grid, change CJK punctuation spacing, or flatten the abstract opt-out into body text. Require source-specific class/main mapping and same-content Chinese or bilingual rendering before a fidelity claim.
expectations: The extractor retains section docGrid attributes and direct paragraph/style grid overrides as distinct source evidence.
An explicit snapToGrid=0 remains a local opt-out rather than being omitted as false-like metadata.
The generated candidate does not automatically install an arbitrary global CJK grid or substitute ordinary line spacing for the Word grid.
The audit remains needs_mapping until a role-specific implementation has same-content rendering evidence.

evals.name: word-theme-colors-and-fonts-remain-role-local-evidence
evals.prompt: A Word template's theme1.xml defines accent1 as 4472C4 and minor Latin as Calibri. A visible footer DOI uses themeColor=accent1 with themeShade=BF, while a named title style uses asciiTheme=majorHAnsi. Explain the required reconstruction behavior.
evals.expected_output: Record document.theme with the raw theme palette/font scheme and each visible or named-style use, including accent1, the BF shade, and majorHAnsi. Write word-theme.tex as evidence. Map the footer DOI and title style separately to source-specific LaTeX interfaces, retaining the aliases and role boundaries. Do not reduce themeColor to auto, substitute the generic Office palette/font globally, or claim a matching LaTeX color/font without same-content render confirmation.
expectations: Theme palette/font definitions and per-span or named-style aliases are preserved separately from resolved local formatting.
Tint and shade attributes remain explicit evidence rather than being silently dropped.
The generated candidate is non-auto-input and the audit remains needs_mapping until a role-specific LaTeX choice is verified.
A generic Office theme is never presented as a journal-specific LaTeX default.

evals.name: theme-evidence-is-bounded-without-losing-audit-provenance
evals.prompt: A 40-page Word template inherits the same minorHAnsi and text1 theme aliases on 800 body runs, while a footer DOI and three title styles use distinct theme combinations. The source inventory records every span. Explain how the generated spec and evidence package should preserve this information for an LLM reconstruction task.
evals.expected_output: Keep every original run and style use in source_inventory.json. In template_spec.json and word-theme.tex, expose bounded review groups keyed by evidence kind, source scope/part/style/container, and exact theme color/font aliases; retain each group's occurrence count and representative locations. Keep the footer DOI and each title style separate from ordinary body inheritance. Do not emit 800 apparent formatting decisions, erase the raw spans, merge furniture into body text, or infer a global LaTeX font/color from the repeated aliases.
expectations: The source inventory remains the authoritative per-span evidence record.
The model-facing spec and generated candidate use bounded role-aware groups with counts and examples.
Grouping never crosses source scope, part, named style, table container, or exact theme alias boundaries.
Repeated inherited aliases do not justify a generic Office palette or global LaTeX font choice.

evals.name: run-level-snap-to-grid-is-a-local-cjk-layout-policy
evals.prompt: A mixed Chinese-English Word template has docGrid type=lines, and its body runs inherit snapToGrid=1 while an English DOI run in the footer has direct w:snapToGrid=0. Explain how the skill must extract and reconstruct this evidence.
evals.expected_output: Record the section grid and the run-level policies as page.text_grid evidence. Keep the footer scope, part, style/container, direct false value, and its local span boundary distinct from body runs. Keep raw spans in source_inventory.json and use a bounded grouped summary with counts and representative locations in text-grid.tex. Do not flatten the footer opt-out into a paragraph rule, treat false as absent, turn it into a font setting, or automatically enable a global CJK baseline grid.
expectations: The extractor models run-level snapToGrid separately from paragraph/style grid policy and removes it from the generic unmodeled-property queue.
False remains an explicit local opt-out when a source grid system is relevant.
Grouping preserves source scope, part, style/container, effective policy, occurrence count, and representative span locations while raw boundaries remain available.
The candidate remains evidence-only until role-specific same-content rendering verifies a LaTeX grid implementation.

evals.name: run-language-complex-script-and-rtl-remain-role-local
evals.prompt: A Word journal template uses lang=en-US across ordinary body runs. A footer publisher name has lang=ar-SA, rtl=1, bCs=1, and a named author style has iCs=1 with an East Asian language slot. Explain the required Temp2TeX reconstruction behavior.
evals.expected_output: Record the body, footer, and named-style values as separate run.script_language evidence groups, retaining direct/effective properties, scope/part/style/container, occurrence counts, and representative raw span locations. Write script-language.tex as evidence while retaining complete boundaries in source_inventory.json. Do not make the entire document RTL, apply Arabic/CJK fonts globally, infer a global Babel/polyglossia/fontspec policy from en-US, or treat complex-script bold/italic as ordinary Latin emphasis. Apply any engine, font, direction, or hyphenation rule only to the confirmed source role after same-content rendering.
expectations: The extractor models lang, bCs, iCs, cs, and rtl as a run-level evidence system rather than leaving them in generic unmodeled properties.
Raw source span boundaries and named styles remain auditable while the model receives bounded role-aware review groups.
A language alias or RTL marker never silently changes document-wide engine, font, language, direction, or hyphenation policy.
Coverage remains needs_mapping until a source-role LaTeX implementation and role-matched rendering justify it.

evals.name: paragraph-bidi-and-text-direction-remain-local-layout-evidence
evals.prompt: A Word template has normal left-to-right body paragraphs. A table-cell paragraph style sets w:bidi=1, and a boxed side note sets w:textDirection=tbRl. Its Arabic publisher name run separately uses w:rtl=1. Explain the required reconstruction behavior.
evals.expected_output: Record paragraph bidi/text-direction as paragraph.direction evidence separate from run.script_language. Preserve the table and side-note containers, direct/effective values, representative paragraph locations, and raw paragraph records. Write paragraph-direction.tex as evidence and map only role-local alignment, start/end indentation, and direction interfaces after same-content rendering. Keep the Arabic run in script-language.tex. Do not make the entire document RTL or vertical, turn paragraph direction into a font choice, treat w:bidi=1 as run-level RTL, or discard a false/default direction record without classifying it.
expectations: The extractor models paragraph bidi and textDirection separately from run-level RTL and removes both nodes from the generic paragraph-property queue.
Active source direction produces a role-local candidate and a needs_mapping coverage gate; disabled/default observations remain auditable but nonblocking.
Grouping preserves scope, part, style/table container, direction values, counts, and representative locations while raw paragraphs remain accessible.
No document-wide RTL, vertical-writing, font, or engine change is inferred without role-matched same-content rendering.

evals.name: paragraph-hyphenation-and-wrap-policy-remains-role-local
evals.prompt: A Word journal template's body and reference styles have w:suppressAutoHyphens=1. A narrow table-cell instruction paragraph has w:wordWrap=0, while ordinary body text relies on Word defaults. Explain the required reconstruction behavior.
evals.expected_output: Record the body/reference and table-cell policies as separate paragraph.break_policy evidence groups with scope, style/container, direct/effective values, counts, representative paragraphs, and raw source records. Write paragraph-break-policy.tex as evidence. Keep active no-hyphenation/no-wrap rules as needs_mapping until same-content line-break and pagination comparison validates a role-local LaTeX interface. Do not apply a global hyphenation penalty, sloppy/nowrap/ragged setting, discard permissive defaults, or treat a table-cell policy as the whole manuscript policy.

evals.name: bounded-atomic-batch-never-hands-off-pending-decisions

evals.name: split-inline-template-instructions-from-visible-structural-labels
evals.prompt: An official Word template has one paragraph with two runs: `ABSTRACT:` followed by `The abstract should not exceed 300 words and should not contain citations. evals.name: distant-caption-candidate-never-becomes-figure-caption-evidence

expectations: Only adjacent or nearby, directionally unambiguous Word object-caption relations can set a source caption position.

Anchored objects with unresolved relations remain outside the generic journalfigure mapping until their role is rendered and confirmed.

evals.name: graphics-insensitive-pdf-comparison-keeps-image-geometry-as-a-separate-gate

evals.name: partial-zone-header-comparison-cannot-promote-class-wide-calibration

evals.name: active-word-footer-rule-remains-full-width-in-two-column-latex

The agent distinguishes a source-backed editable rule value from unverified section-specific placement or a full-fidelity claim.

evals.name: regression-fixture-preserves-official-multicols-body-wrapper

evals.name: first-page-logo-and-even-furniture-need-composition-and-twoside
evals.prompt: A Word template has a first-page publisher logo immediately beside five masthead lines, then a multi-line publication footer. Its default header has a title and page number, while the even header has author names and a page number. Word does not set mirror margins. The generated LaTeX compiles, but the logo replaces the masthead text and the even header is absent. What must Temp2TeX change before calling this a candidate?

Re-render page 1 and one odd/even later-page pair; do not claim fidelity merely because the document compiles. Keep exact logo baseline, rule geometry, and page-relative placement as render-calibration decisions.

A distinct even Word variant triggers twoside LaTeX class behavior independently of mirror margins.

evals.name: readable-word-furniture-remains-inactive-until-explicit-promotion

Generate a separate text-only or text-plus-asset candidate only after the model has selected the intended Word variants for comparison; promotion requires rendered page 1 and, when applicable, odd/even later-page evidence.

The response distinguishes a text-only candidate from a candidate that also activates header/footer artwork.

evals.name: local-furniture-contract-rejects-presence-with-wrong-placement
evals.prompt: A generated first page contains the correct journal name, ISSN, publisher logo, and online-publication text. A comparison against the rendered Word template shows the logo box is aligned within 1pt, but the three masthead text lines are 42pt too low and the online-publication text is 287pt too low. Bind unique journal and footer phrases to their source page rectangles, set conservative per-anchor placement tolerances, and require the logo image box separately. The image-box check may pass while the text anchors fail; record a failed local-zone gate with the named displacement evidence. Keep the corrected furniture as a candidate, do not promote it to the ordinary class, and do not use this local result to tune body margins or typography. Image pixels are not compared, but the image frame and its relationship to masthead text are verified.
expectations: The agent distinguishes content presence from source-relative placement.
The agent separately reports text-anchor tolerance failures and image-box geometry results.

evals.name: logo-text-pair-uses-top-alignment-and-nonadditive-height
evals.prompt: A first-page Word masthead has a 49pt logo to the left of five journal-information lines. A generated fancyhdr candidate preserves both, but the text begins at the bottom of the logo and the article title is pushed down by about 50pt because the header height equals logo height plus every text line. What should Temp2TeX change, and what remains render-gated?

Re-render the local first-page zone and check the logo frame independently from every masthead phrase. Keep baseline, rules, title-to-masthead distance, and a multi-line first-page footer render-gated. A footer that appears above the physical page bottom may need a separate positioned first-page block; do not call a generic fancyfoot reconstruction faithful just because the text exists.
expectations: The agent identifies baseline alignment and additive header height as distinct causes.
The agent retains logo and text as separate editable fields while composing them visually.
The response does not promote a first-page footer without source-relative rendered placement evidence.

evals.name: legacy-doc-collapsed-right-tab-remains-a-render-gated-candidate
evals.prompt: A converted legacy DOC first-page header has a fifth line with two separate text runs: `Volume ..., Pages ...` followed by 36 spaces and `ISSN: 1234-5678`. The active paragraph no longer exposes a right-tab node, but the rendered Word page places the ISSN at the far right. How should Temp2TeX reconstruct and verify it?
evals.expected_output: Treat the separated runs and unusually long whitespace as degraded tab evidence, not ordinary prose. Generate an editable single-line candidate that keeps the left text and right ISSN in a fixed-width line with a right-extending fill, preserving local run formatting. Do not infer this from normal spaces or general body text. Compare the two endpoint boxes against the rendered Word page and keep the candidate unpromoted if either placement exceeds its local-zone tolerance.

evals.name: local-contract-distinguishes-page-fixed-and-flow-relative-blocks
evals.prompt: A Word template stores a publisher citation and online-publication block in `footer1.xml`, while correspondence text appears below the author affiliations in the document body. The generated PDF uses a shorter abstract, so the correspondence moves upward by 36pt, but the footer is 120pt too low. How should Temp2TeX choose and interpret local comparison contracts?
evals.expected_output: Classify the footer as `page_fixed`: bind its unique phrases to a first-page rectangle and use absolute placement tolerances. Its 120pt displacement is a failed furniture gate and cannot be excused by the shorter body. Classify correspondence as `flow_relative`: bind it to a unique title or affiliation context anchor, compare its context-relative box with a declared tolerance, and require both context and correspondence to be on the same page in each PDF. Do not use either local result to tune global body density, margins, pagination, or unrelated furniture. Missing context or a cross-page relation is a failed flow-context gate, not a reason to fall back to absolute coordinates.
expectations: The footer is classified from its Word part ownership as page-fixed, not from the body PDF flow.
Correspondence uses a context-relative contract with same-page context checks.
A body-flow change cannot excuse an absolute page-furniture mismatch.
Neither local result is promoted into a global calibration claim.

evals.name: page-frame-probe-rejects-partial-or-unstable-comparison
evals.prompt: A PDF profiler reports a 9pt right-edge difference. Its anchor map is `partial_zone` for the first-page masthead, the generated document has one fewer page, and the masthead text itself exceeds its local placement tolerance. May Temp2TeX run a page-margin candidate from this report?
evals.expected_output: No. A page-frame probe requires a full-document same-content contract, equal page counts, complete anchors with no page shifts, no failed local gate, and at least two pages whose text-box edge deltas are directionally consistent. This report is only a local furniture diagnosis, so `suggest_page_calibration.py` must return `not_eligible` with the contract and page-flow reasons. Repair the named furniture or fixture/flow problem first; do not materialize or promote a margin candidate.
expectations: The agent refuses to derive global margins from a partial-zone comparison.
Page-count mismatch and failed local furniture placement remain separate blocking reasons.
The response requires a complete multi-page same-content contract before a page-frame probe.
The agent does not materialize or promote a rejected proposal.

evals.name: visual-repair-plan-preserves-dependency-order
evals.prompt: A completed atomic audit and successful compile are available. The full same-content PDF comparison has an extra generated page, shifted reference and appendix anchors, and a visual report that also lists body-density and page-frame causes. What should Temp2TeX do next?

Inspect source-backed section breaks, front-matter/body column transition, float and caption flow, and back-matter or appendix boundaries; repair one identified flow boundary and rerender the same fixture. Do not run page-margin or body-font calibration while page count or anchor pages differ, and do not turn the multi-cause visual score into a parameter search.
expectations: The agent uses structural flow as the first visual-repair concern when page count or anchor pages differ.
The response names source-backed flow evidence rather than guessing margins or font size.
Page-frame and body-density calibration stay blocked until structural flow is repaired.

evals.name: global-calibration-hints-stay-blocked-during-flow-failure
evals.prompt: The full same-content report has matching anchor text but the generated PDF has three pages while the reference has two, and the figure anchor moved to the next page. The profiler also measures a 0.9pt smaller median font and 1.2pt tighter line gap. What may Temp2TeX calibrate next?
evals.expected_output: Nothing global. The report must mark `global_calibration_eligible: false` and suppress font, baseline, line-gap, and page-frame calibration hints. The next action is a source-backed structural-flow review of the relevant front-matter boundary, float/caption policy, forced break, or back-matter transition. Rerender the same fixture after one identified flow repair; only a same-page, same-count result can enable a global calibration proposal.
expectations: The response treats page-count or anchor-page drift as a hard block on global calibration.
The response does not use measured font or line-gap differences to start a probe while structural flow is unresolved.
The next action is limited to one source-backed flow boundary investigation and rerender.

evals.name: visual-repair-plan-returns-bounded-word-evidence-readback
evals.prompt: A full same-content comparison has one extra generated page and only the figure anchor moved to the next page. A current ledger-matched atomic audit is available. What evidence should the next Temp2TeX agent review before changing the class?
evals.expected_output: Read `visual_repair_plan.evidence_review_scope`. For this structural-flow case it must select page-frame and page-column evidence plus figure-placement and figure-caption audit units, and then inspect the immediately adjacent Word paragraphs at those figure boundaries. It must expose the matching evidence IDs and a role-filtered readback command. It must not open a generic body-paragraph review, tune margins/fonts, or treat a stale audit as evidence; a fingerprint-mismatched audit requires refresh first.
expectations: The response uses the repair scope rather than a free-form PDF-based guess.
The structural-flow scope is bounded to page setup and the actually shifted figure role, with adjacent boundary paragraphs.
The response identifies fingerprint mismatch as a block on source-rule selection.
The response still changes at most one source-backed boundary after review.

evals.name: direct-word-format-needs-property-level-latex-binding
evals.prompt: A Word title run has direct `font.bold=true`, `font.size_half_points=26`, and `font.color=4472C4`. The agent marks it mapped to `front_matter.title` and points `latex_token` at `\maketitle`, but records no property bindings. Is the atomic audit complete?
evals.expected_output: No. A mapped/default unit with direct Word formatting must include `format_bindings` for every `direct_format` leaf. Each binding must repeat the exact source path and value, point to a package-local executable LaTeX token, and state the transformation reason, such as 26 half-points to 13pt, bold to `\bfseries`, or the source color to a named color declaration. The strict audit must reject a generic owner token without these records. These bindings are traceability evidence, not a substitute for the role-level render check.
expectations: The response requires one binding per direct Word format leaf, not only one role-level token.
Every binding preserves source path and exact source value, executable package token, and transformation reason.
The response treats missing bindings as a strict-audit failure and does not overclaim visual fidelity.

evals.name: binding-review-draft-preserves-exact-word-values
evals.prompt: A model opens a bounded atomic-mapping batch for a title run whose direct Word properties are bold=true, family=Palatino Linotype, and size_half_points=32. What should the Temp2TeX batch draft contain, and what may the model edit?
evals.expected_output: The review sheet and batch draft must already list one `format_bindings` object per direct property with the exact `source_path` and `source_value`: true, Palatino Linotype, and 32. The model fills only package-local `latex_file`, executable `latex_token`, and `mapping_reason` for each binding, plus the final role/owner decision. It must not overwrite the source values, omit a binding, or merge the batch while a binding token/reason remains blank; the guarded merger and strict audit reject it.
expectations: The response keeps exact Word values immutable in the model-facing draft.
The response limits model edits to LaTeX ownership and transformation explanation fields.
The response identifies incomplete bindings as a guarded-merge and strict-audit failure.

evals.name: observable-word-object-layout-needs-property-level-binding
evals.prompt: A Word figure is an anchored drawing with a source width and height, margin-relative horizontal offset, paragraph-relative vertical offset, `wrapNone`, and nonzero left/right wrap distances. The agent maps it to `figure.placement` and points only to a generic `\begin{figure}` token. Can strict audit accept it?
evals.expected_output: No. The drawing is an observable object-layout unit and must include `object_format_bindings` for every retained geometry/structure field: dimensions, anchor/relative positions, offsets, wrap mode and distances, overlap/behind state where present, plus direct surrounding paragraph formatting. Each binding preserves the exact source path and value and names an executable package-local LaTeX token with a transformation reason. The audit may omit source relationship bookkeeping, inherited paragraph values, and duplicate width/height copies, but it must not treat a generic float token as proof of placement fidelity. Render comparison remains required before promotion.
expectations: The response distinguishes object-layout bindings from ordinary paragraph/run bindings.
The response preserves visible drawing geometry and filters only source identity, inherited paragraph values, and duplicate native dimensions.
The response rejects a generic figure token as sufficient evidence and retains render verification.

evals.name: object-review-selects-correct-render-model-and-image-policy
evals.prompt: A Word ledger has an inline body figure with no confirmed nearby caption, a table with a distant caption candidate, and an anchored logo in the first-page header. How should Temp2TeX prepare their PDF verification?
evals.expected_output: The body figure and table receive flow-relative review requirements: choose a unique rendered caption or nearby non-generic manuscript context only after the same-content PDF pair exists, require object/context same-page relation, and inspect caption order, object-facing gaps, outside spacing, and surrounding flow. Because their Word caption candidates are unconfirmed/distant, do not use them as anchors automatically. The header logo receives a page-fixed first-page contract for its artwork frame and adjacent furniture, independent of body flow. Mask only the figure/logo raster interiors; continue checking their boxes, captions, wrapping, whitespace, and all table text/rules.
expectations: The response chooses flow-relative versus page-fixed validation from object ownership and flow.
The response does not promote distant/unknown caption evidence into an automatic anchor.
The response masks image interiors only and retains image-frame, caption, table, and flow verification.

evals.name: regression-keeps-pending-word-mapping-separate-from-not-comparable
evals.prompt: A regression case has a valid official Word source, a compiled generated LaTeX PDF, and a usable Word-render reference, but its fresh atomic audit still has pending paragraph/run and object decisions. How must Temp2TeX report the case?
evals.expected_output: Report `pending_atomic_audit`, retain the compiled artifacts and any base diagnostic information, and block calibration, probe promotion, visual-match claims, and strict pass. The benchmark must place it in a separate incomplete/pending bucket rather than `failed_or_not_comparable`; `not_comparable` is reserved for unavailable or incompatible source/reference evidence. The runner should still return nonzero until the audit is complete, so the incomplete training state cannot be treated as success.
expectations: The response distinguishes pending source mapping from reference comparability.
The response preserves the nonzero incomplete signal while avoiding a false source-failure count.
The response blocks calibration and strict fidelity claims until the atomic audit completes.

evals.name: reconciliation-requeues-legacy-decisions-without-property-bindings
evals.prompt: A regenerated Word ledger has the same evidence ID, candidate role, and direct drawing geometry as an older atomic decision. The old decision is `mapped` to `figure.placement`, but it predates `object_format_bindings` and contains none. How should Temp2TeX reconcile and audit it?
evals.expected_output: Run `reconcile_atomic_mapping_decisions.py` and requeue this group as `pending`, recording it in `binding_migration_required_keys`. Preserve the fresh ledger's immutable source paths and exact geometry values, then complete `object_format_bindings` with package-local executable LaTeX tokens and transformation reasons in a bounded review batch. Do not copy the old mapped status back merely because the source identity still matches. Strict audit should treat it as an unfinished decision, not manufacture an `invalid_decision` wall from a legacy schema; it remains a block on fidelity until the new bindings are completed.
expectations: The response distinguishes source-identity reconciliation from schema/binding migration.
The legacy final decision returns to pending while exact current Word values remain immutable and available for review.
The response requires completion of the new direct/object binding records and blocks fidelity promotion until then.

evals.name: central-text-extent-cannot-alone-trigger-page-margin-calibration
evals.prompt: A full same-content PDF comparison reports a 28pt narrower central text extent. However, the Introduction and Methods anchors have less than 2pt horizontal drift, References moved to a later page, and the central range includes a title block and a floating figure. What should Temp2TeX diagnose and do next?
evals.expected_output: Do not label this a confirmed page-frame mismatch and do not propose a margin edit. The central-band range is coarse diagnostic evidence only; page-frame investigation requires at least two same-page manuscript-body anchors with a stable horizontal shift. Here the body anchors do not corroborate it and References has a structural-flow shift. Repair the source-backed flow/object or front-matter boundary first, then rerender. The report may retain the central extent as an unattributed review signal, but it cannot enable a global page-frame or body-density calibration.
expectations: The response distinguishes central content extent from corroborated manuscript-body geometry.
The response requires repeated same-page body-anchor evidence before a page-frame route is selected.
The response resolves the observed structural flow or role-local cause before any global calibration.

evals.name: mapped-class-macro-must-be-used-not-merely-declared
evals.prompt: A model maps a Word title's direct bold format to the journalTitleStyle macro in journal-template.cls. The class declares that macro with newcommand, but neither main.tex nor any active class path invokes it. The model says the strict audit should pass because the token exists outside comments. Is that valid?
evals.expected_output: No. A declared but unused class macro is not active template behavior. Strict audit and guarded batch merge must reject a bare .cls macro that appears only in its declaration. The agent must map an actual invocation path, such as the title interface used by main.tex or maketitle, or keep the unit unresolved until that path exists. This static use check improves traceability but does not replace the same-content render check. Direct class-load statements such as setlength remain valid active declaration targets.

The response requires a non-declaration package use before mapped/default acceptance.
The response distinguishes this static activation guard from render-fidelity proof and permits direct class-load declarations.

evals.name: legacy-word-input-preserves-authority-and-openxml-dot-skips-conversion
evals.prompt: A publisher provides a binary .doc template and a second file whose URL ends in .dot but whose package contents are OpenXML. LibreOffice is available. How should Temp2TeX inspect these sources before building the Word format ledger?
evals.expected_output: Inspect file contents before trusting the suffix. For the true binary .doc, retain the original as the authority, use LibreOffice only to create a temporary DOCX for structured inspection, and record converted_for_inspection provenance in the ledger, including converter details and the limitation that the temporary DOCX enabled extraction. For the OpenXML .dot, parse it directly as OpenXML with no unnecessary conversion and do not falsely call it a legacy binary. Both paths still require the normal atom-level mapping audit before ordinary delivery; successful conversion or compilation is not a fidelity pass.
expectations: The response distinguishes payload detection from filename extension.
The binary source remains authoritative and conversion provenance is preserved.
The OpenXML .dot avoids redundant conversion, and neither route is treated as completed without atomic mapping.

evals.name: rtf-input-keeps-original-authority-and-renderer-provenance
evals.prompt: A journal supplies only an official .rtf author template. LibreOffice can convert it to DOCX and render it to PDF, but Microsoft Word is unavailable. How should Temp2TeX extract, build, and verify the resulting LaTeX template?
evals.expected_output: Treat the original RTF as the authoritative official source. Use LibreOffice only to create a temporary DOCX for the paragraph/run ledger and record `source_conversion.status=converted_for_inspection`, the converter, and the original source kind. Build the usual atomic mapping queue and editable `.cls + main.tex` package from that evidence. A LibreOffice PDF may serve as an available same-content comparison reference, but its renderer provenance and Word-fidelity limitation must remain in the report; do not claim it is a Microsoft Word render or substitute successful conversion/compilation for the atomic audit.
expectations: The response preserves the RTF original as authority and records LibreOffice conversion as a temporary inspection bridge.
The response keeps renderer provenance explicit and does not call a LibreOffice PDF a Word render.
The response requires ordinary atomic mapping and audit before fidelity claims.

evals.name: atomic-review-cards-preserve-local-word-context-and-final-status
evals.prompt: A model opens a bounded review batch for a Word affiliation run whose isolated text is `Address of Author 1`. Its parent paragraph is between the author line and two alternate affiliation placeholders, uses a named style, and has direct line-spacing evidence. Another selected group is already mapped. What must the Temp2TeX review card and batch draft do?
evals.expected_output: The review card must show the immutable evidence ID and direct-format bindings plus read-only local Word context: parent paragraph text, nearby preceding/following paragraphs, named style, table-cell state, and paragraph-level direct format. Context scanning stops at a table-cell or container boundary, so a later body paragraph cannot leap across a table into the card. This gives the model enough context to distinguish the affiliation placeholder from an author or instruction line without changing Word evidence. The pending group appears in the fingerprint-bound batch draft; the already mapped group does not. Its review instruction is to audit the existing owner, bindings, and active package token, reopening it only for a concrete source or owner conflict rather than reclassifying it merely because the queue was regenerated.
expectations: The response requires read-only neighboring Word context rather than an isolated text fragment and stops it at structural table/container boundaries.
The response preserves evidence IDs and source values while limiting the pending batch to editable final dispositions.
The response distinguishes auditing a final decision from automatically reopening it.

evals.name: pending-only-review-batches-open-work-and-reject-empty-slices
evals.prompt: A conversion readiness report selects `front_matter.affiliation` as the next mapping slice. The decision file has three affiliation groups still pending and two already final. What review command and behavior should Temp2TeX use? What if a later run finds that all five are final?
evals.expected_output: Use `prepare_atomic_mapping_review.py` with the selected `--roles`, `--pending-only`, a stable batch size/index, and a fingerprint-bound batch-template output. The review card and update draft include only the three pending groups; final groups remain available to the normal review/audit path but are not reclassified or placed in an active mapping batch. If a later run finds no pending group in the requested slice, the command must stop with an instruction to omit `--pending-only` only for a concrete final mapping audit or to select the next readiness-recommended pending slice. It must not emit an empty task that invites the model to invent work.
expectations: The response uses pending-only mode for an active continuation batch.
The response keeps final groups out of the pending batch while retaining their audit path.
The response rejects an empty pending-only slice instead of fabricating a model task.

evals.name: phased-skill-loading-keeps-ordinary-conversion-on-evidence-path
evals.prompt: A user provides one official DOCX author template, a journal author-instructions page, and a sample PDF. They ask for an editable LaTeX template, not a skill benchmark. How should an agent load and apply Temp2TeX without being overwhelmed by implementation detail or drifting into corpus work?

Build the class-based package, use language defaults only for documented gaps, and run the verification checklist after mapping and compilation. The response keeps the ordinary task out of full-corpus regression and preserves source/default/gap provenance.

evals.name: readiness-never-offers-atomic-mapping-before-system-triage
evals.prompt: A current v3 Word ledger has complete paragraph/run capture and a pending atomic audit, but it also contains document-grid and character-style aggregate evidence. `system_format_triage.json` is absent. What must conversion readiness report? What changes after a ledger-fingerprint-matched triage queue is created?

expectations: The response prevents a system-triage phase from emitting an ordinary mapping slice.
The response uses a ledger-fingerprint-matched triage queue as the transition prerequisite.
The response distinguishes entering atomic mapping from completing the child-level system audit.

evals.name: system-triage-child-batches-keep-aggregate-evidence-auditable
evals.prompt: A Word ledger contains one section text grid, seven local text-grid overrides, and 83 grouped script/language samples. A previous `system_format_triage.json` already has some final child decisions. How should an agent review the remaining system evidence without resetting its decisions or treating either aggregate as one global LaTeX setting?

Preserve existing child IDs and immutable source evidence; final children stay out of the pending view unless there is a concrete conflict. Edit the matching JSON child, not the aggregate summary, then rerun strict atomic audit. A batch sheet is review context and never automatically approves, closes, or reopens a disposition.
expectations: The response rejects childless aggregate triage and does not turn a text grid or inherited language metadata into a document-wide LaTeX rule.
The response preserves final decisions through a matching existing queue and uses stable pending-only batches for bounded model work.
The response requires a child-level strict audit after decisions, distinguishing evidence review from visual approval.

evals.name: system-aggregates-never-reenter-ordinary-atomic-mapping
evals.prompt: A Word ledger contains document-grid, tab-stop, character-effect, character-style, script/language, and paragraph hyphenation/wrap aggregate evidence. An older atomic decision file still includes pending groups for text-grid, script-language, and paragraph-break policy. How must the model split and review this work without creating a global LaTeX setting or duplicating audit responsibility?
