Strict audit checks the child records and rejects missing, stale, childless, or unresolved system triage.
expectations: The response distinguishes system child triage from ordinary paragraph/run/object mapping and prevents duplicate decisions.
The response includes paragraph break policy alongside grid and script/language evidence, with no document-wide default inferred from an aggregate.
The response preserves child provenance and requires strict audit rather than treating a batch or generic class macro as completion.

evals.name: system-child-mapping-requires-an-active-latex-token
evals.prompt: A system-triage child for an explicit Word text-grid opt-out is marked `default` and names `\journalgridpolicy` in `journal-template.cls`. That macro is declared but never invoked anywhere in the package. Can strict audit accept the child? What changes if the macro is actually invoked from the class?
evals.expected_output: Strict audit must reject the declared-only bare macro. A mapped/default system child needs an executable local owner token, not a token that only appears in a definition. The child must remain unresolved or point to the active invocation. Once a non-declaration package use invokes the macro, the traceability check may pass, provided the child still has a valid source disposition, owner, file, token, and any required linked ordinary mapping. This does not replace role-matched rendering where the source effect is visually active.
expectations: The response rejects a bare system-child macro with declaration-only evidence.
The response distinguishes active token traceability from visual fidelity proof.
The response keeps the child unresolved rather than inventing a global formatting rule.

evals.name: linked-system-child-still-needs-local-owner-and-reason
evals.prompt: A text-grid child links to an ordinary Word run that is already mapped. The child is marked `default` but contains no reason, LaTeX owner, file, or token. May strict audit accept it because the ordinary run is mapped?
evals.expected_output: No. The ordinary link is traceability, not the system child's mapping. A final mapped/default child needs its own concise source reason and a package-local owner, file, and active token; if it has a link, the linked ordinary unit must also be mapped/default. This prevents inherited language, grid, theme, or line-break evidence from being silently absorbed into a generic paragraph/run mapping. The agent must add a local executable policy or leave the child unresolved.
expectations: The response rejects a linked child with missing local owner/token/reason.
The response distinguishes a link's traceability function from source-property implementation.
The response requires an active package token or a documented unresolved state.

evals.name: system-triage-child-edit-invalidates-old-atomic-audit
evals.prompt: A Word package has a v2 system triage queue and an atomic audit with the same Word ledger fingerprint. After that audit, an agent changes only the reason on one system child. May it retain the old audit, refresh coverage, or continue with an ordinary mapping batch?
evals.expected_output: No. The atomic audit must bind the exact serialized system triage queue, not just the Word ledger. Any child edit makes the prior audit stale, even if the child ID, ledger fingerprint, and status are unchanged. Readiness must enter `system_triage_audit_refresh`, emit no normal mapping slice, and require a strict audit rerun before coverage refresh, package validation, visual calibration, or a fidelity claim. The validator must reject the stale audit. A v1 queue, or a queue missing required text-grid, tab-stop, paragraph-break, character, script/language, theme, or unmodeled-property evidence, is not acceptable for ordinary delivery.
expectations: The response rejects ledger-only freshness as insufficient after a child-triage edit.
The response names the audit-refresh phase and prevents a normal mapping slice from appearing there.
The response requires v2 triage and includes tab-stop and paragraph-break evidence in the validation gate.

evals.name: image-content-mask-preserves-frame-caption-and-table-evidence
evals.prompt: A same-content PDF comparison contains a figure whose raster pixels differ between Word and LaTeX, but the generated figure has no border and its caption/table alignment may also differ. What may the image-insensitive comparison mask, and what must remain auditable?
evals.expected_output: Mask only the raster artwork interior. Preserve a narrow image perimeter in the format metric so border/frame differences remain visible, and compare image box position, dimensions, and aspect ratio separately. Never mask the caption, caption spacing/order/typography, surrounding whitespace, table rules/cells/text, or downstream flow. The report must record the retained frame-band width and graphic geometry result. A lower pixel score obtained by masking a whole figure box is not a template-fidelity pass.
expectations: The response limits masking to artwork interiors and explicitly retains frame/perimeter evidence.
The response keeps caption and table evidence outside every image mask.
The response treats graphic geometry and page flow as independent checks rather than pixel content.

evals.name: stale-system-triage-audit-cannot-drive-visual-repair
evals.prompt: A comparable PDF pair reports a body-density or caption-flow difference. Its atomic audit matches the Word ledger, but a system-triage child was changed after the audit. May the agent use the old audit's evidence IDs to choose a visual repair probe?
evals.expected_output: No. A visual repair scope is source evidence only when both the Word ledger and the exact current system-triage queue match the strict audit. The scope must return `audit_triage_mismatch`, prohibit calibration/probe selection, and require a strict audit refresh first. The model must not use a plausible PDF difference to bypass a later child-level correction or compensate with global font, margin, or float tuning.
expectations: The response applies triage freshness to visual repair, not only package handoff.
The response names `audit_triage_mismatch` and requires strict audit refresh before a probe.
The response prevents global visual tuning from bypassing child evidence.

evals.name: unmodeled-ooxml-aggregate-expands-to-node-level-triage
evals.prompt: A Word ledger contains object evidence `word.unmodeled-format-properties.system`. Its captured properties are `w:noProof` and `w:adjustRightInd`. The system-triage producer creates records ending in `.noProof` and `.adjustRightInd`. What must strict audit require, and may an agent add one synthetic `.system` triage record to make the audit pass?
evals.expected_output: Strict audit expands the ledger aggregate into the concrete node record IDs `word.unmodeled-format-properties.noProof` and `word.unmodeled-format-properties.adjustRightInd`. Each node record must contain its own child dispositions and provenance. It must not require or accept a synthetic `.system` triage record, because that would merge different OOXML behaviors and bypass node-level review. The aggregate remains excluded from ordinary atomic paragraph/run mapping; if the ledger lists the aggregate but supplies no inspectable property nodes, strict audit fails conservatively rather than treating it as complete.
expectations: The response distinguishes a ledger aggregate signal from node-level strict-audit requirements.
The response requires separate evidence-bound dispositions for `w:noProof` and `w:adjustRightInd`.
The response rejects a synthetic aggregate record and keeps malformed aggregate evidence conservatively unresolved.

evals.name: visual-repair-plan-receives-current-system-triage
evals.prompt: A package has a comparable PDF report and a current `system_format_triage.json`. The readiness tool creates a visual repair plan whose evidence scope must reject a stale atomic audit after a system-child edit. What context must the planner receive, and what is the required behavior?
evals.expected_output: The readiness path must pass the current system-triage document into the visual repair planner and then into its evidence-scope check. The planner must run without a missing-variable/runtime failure. If the audit's system-triage fingerprint differs from the current queue, the scope returns `audit_triage_mismatch`, blocks source-rule selection and render probes, and requires a strict audit refresh. A ledger fingerprint alone is not sufficient.
expectations: The response requires explicit current-triage parameter flow into visual-repair evidence selection.
The response identifies the stale-triage audit gate rather than allowing a visual repair probe.
The response treats missing runtime context as an implementation defect, not as permission to bypass the audit.

evals.name: object-anchor-uses-exact-word-evidence-ids
evals.prompt: A journal Word template contains two tables. A same-content PDF report identifies a visual discrepancy at `table_1`, whose custom anchor map declares `source_evidence_ids: ["table.t001.structure", "p0031"]`. What source review may the agent perform, and what happens if either ID is absent from the current ledger-matched atomic audit?
evals.expected_output: The agent uses the exact object/caption evidence IDs and the readiness-provided `--evidence-ids` review path, then inspects only that table, its caption, and the immediate source-flow context. It does not review or alter the second table merely because both share a role. The IDs must come from the current ledger/audit and are retained in the layout profile's `anchor_source_evidence_ids`. If the audit does not contain a requested ID, readiness returns `no_matching_evidence_ids`; the agent repairs the anchor contract or refreshes the audit and must not broaden back to every table/figure role.
expectations: The response binds an object-specific PDF anchor to immutable current Word evidence IDs.
The response scopes source review to the exact object/caption context instead of all objects with the same role.
The response rejects a missing evidence ID without role-wide fallback or global layout tuning.

evals.name: object-review-emits-source-backed-anchor-candidates
evals.prompt: A Word drawing has `drawing_ordinal: 1`, evidence ID `figure.d001.placement`, and an adjacent below caption at paragraph 21: `Figure 1. Caption of Figure 1.` The review queue also records the caption's paragraph index. What should the object review card emit, and what must the agent still verify before using it?
evals.expected_output: The review card marks the caption source-confirmed and emits an `anchor_contract_candidates` entry with key `figure_1`, the caption phrase, and source evidence IDs `figure.d001.placement` plus `p0021`. It records the source caption position and says the candidate requires a uniqueness check in both same-content PDFs. The agent may add the candidate to a task anchor map only after that PDF check; it must not claim a page rectangle, reuse the candidate after the Word ledger changes, or invent a candidate when no confirmed caption relation exists.
expectations: The response uses the ledger's actual `caption_text` and caption paragraph index rather than a nonexistent alternate field.
The response emits a per-object candidate with both object and caption provenance.
The response retains PDF uniqueness confirmation as a gate before anchor-contract use.

evals.name: duplicate-source-caption-relation-cannot-produce-multiple-auto-anchors
evals.prompt: A Word review group contains `figure.d001.placement` and `figure.d002.placement`. Both objects point to the same adjacent caption phrase, `Figure 1. Caption of Figure 1.`, at paragraph `p0021`. May the review card automatically emit `figure_1` and `figure_2` anchor contracts?
evals.expected_output: No. The repeated source caption phrase makes the object/caption relation ambiguous for automatic anchoring. The card records the ambiguous candidates but emits no auto-usable anchor contract for either object. The agent must choose a unique rendered context phrase and confirm it in both PDFs, or leave the relation unresolved with a gap-log entry. Physical adjacency alone is insufficient evidence for two distinct anchor bindings.
expectations: The response rejects automatic per-object anchors when a caption phrase is reused within the source relation set.
The response preserves the ambiguity for review instead of silently selecting an ordinal-looking binding.
The response requires a unique same-content PDF context or an explicit unresolved gap.

evals.name: caption-relation-prefers-matching-label-and-preserves-unresolved-ties
evals.prompt: A drawing at paragraph 22 is the second body drawing. It has an equal-distance Figure 1 caption above at paragraph 21 and Figure 2 caption below at paragraph 23. Separately, another object has equal-distance unlabelled caption candidates above and below. How must Word evidence extraction classify both cases?
evals.expected_output: For the second drawing, extraction selects the below Figure 2 caption because its visible label matches object ordinal 2, and records `label_match: matched`, source position, and paragraph evidence. It must not use a distance-only earlier-paragraph tie break. For unlabelled equal-distance candidates, extraction returns `confidence: ambiguous` with both candidate records and leaves caption position/object spacing/object-anchor generation unresolved. Chinese visible `表 N` and `图 N` labels are recognized under the same rule.
expectations: The response prioritizes a matching visible caption label over a distance-only tie break.
The response preserves unresolved equal-distance unlabelled candidates rather than inventing a float direction.
The response includes both English and Chinese label recognition.

evals.name: nearby-labelled-caption-with-wrong-ordinal-is-not-confirmed
evals.prompt: The third Word drawing is one paragraph away from a visible `Figure 2` caption. No Figure 3 caption exists nearby. May extraction treat the Figure 2 paragraph as an adjacent caption for drawing 3 because it is close?
evals.expected_output: No. Because a nearby candidate has an explicit label and it does not match source object ordinal 3, extraction returns `confidence: label_mismatch`, `position: unknown`, `label_match: mismatch`, and preserves the candidate as diagnostic context. The relation may not set caption position, object spacing, float placement, or an object-specific PDF anchor. The agent must find matching source evidence or retain an explicit gap; it must not replace the mismatch with a generic nearby relation.
expectations: The response blocks a visibly mismatched candidate despite physical proximity.
The response retains diagnostic provenance instead of silently dropping the candidate.
The response prevents label-mismatched evidence from driving class or PDF-anchor behavior.

evals.name: caption-relation-corpus-audit-blocks-false-layout-training-signal
evals.prompt: A 60-case Word corpus audit reports that the same table/figure caption paragraph is confirmed for multiple object ordinals in five templates. May the model use those cases to tune a global LaTeX caption position or float policy?
evals.expected_output: No. A duplicate confirmed caption assignment is a Word source-extraction defect until resolved. The model runs the caption-relation audit before interpreting regression PDF differences, then fixes the relation or records it as `ambiguous` or `label_mismatch`. It must not treat one caption as evidence for multiple objects, tune global caption/float behavior from those cases, or silently discard the duplicate provenance. This source audit supplements but does not replace same-content PDF comparison.
expectations: The response treats duplicate confirmed relations as failed source evidence, not a template rule.
The response requires resolving or explicitly preserving ambiguity before visual training.
The response distinguishes the source audit from the later same-content PDF gate.

evals.name: caption-audit-disposition-limits-training-decisions
evals.prompt: A corpus caption audit marks one figure as `remote_caption_candidate`, one as `label_mismatch`, one as `no_observed_caption_relation`, and one as `confirmed_source_relation`. A PDF comparison reports object/caption layout differences for all four. Which cases may drive a new class caption-order or float-policy candidate?
evals.expected_output: Only the `confirmed_source_relation` object may produce a bounded candidate for caption order, object-facing spacing, float behavior, or an object-specific PDF anchor, and it still needs the normal same-content render gate. A remote candidate is diagnostic and may support caption typography only if independently selected. Label-mismatched and unobserved relations cannot train caption or float behavior; the agent logs the gaps and seeks rendered Word or independent source evidence. It does not turn the aggregate PDF score into a global rule.
expectations: The response treats evidence disposition as a gate before visual-training interpretation.
The response limits float and caption-order candidates to confirmed source relations.
The response preserves unresolved object relations as gaps instead of averaging them into a publisher-wide class rule.

evals.name: caption-disposition-propagates-from-source-to-spec
evals.prompt: A Word source inventory records a selected table relation as `position: unknown`, `confidence: label_mismatch`, and `evidence_disposition.state: label_mismatch`. A valid figure relation in the same template is `confirmed_source_relation` below its object. How must `template_spec.json` represent the two caption positions?
evals.expected_output: The table must use the documented table default and record the observed label-mismatch relation and a reason that it cannot set caption order. It must not become `status: source` merely because a caption-looking paragraph exists nearby. The figure may retain its below position as source-backed evidence, including the confirmed disposition and source relation provenance. The source inventory, Word ledger, and spec must preserve the same boundary.
expectations: The response requires a confirmed source disposition before a caption position is source-backed.
The response preserves the non-confirmed relation as diagnostic provenance in the default-backed spec entry.
The response distinguishes an independently confirmed figure from a mismatched table in the same Word template.

evals.name: word-capture-completeness-precedes-atomic-mapping
evals.prompt: A Word capture audit reports `capture_complete` with 277 body/table-cell paragraphs, 596 contiguous run spans, headers, footnotes, drawings, and table structures. Another official Word template reports `captured_sparse_or_empty` with no body paragraphs. What may the agent conclude and do next?
evals.expected_output: For the first template, the agent may begin atomic map-or-gap review for each captured paragraph, run, object, and ancillary unit, but must not claim those units are already mapped or visually matched. For the sparse template, it records the lack of visible body evidence, consults official guides/sample PDFs when available, and otherwise uses documented language defaults with a gap log. Neither status authorizes fabricated formatting; only `capture_incomplete` blocks strict mapping and calibration until extraction limitations are fixed.
expectations: The response distinguishes source extraction completeness from mapping completion.
The response treats a sparse official template as an evidence gap, not a reason to invent a body style.
The response preserves strict blocking behavior for actual capture limitations.

evals.name: layout-only-word-runs-cannot-silently-disappear
evals.prompt: A Word header contains a tab run, and a table-cell paragraph contains a non-breaking-space run with direct bold formatting. Neither run has visible letters. May the agent omit them from atomic mapping because their trimmed text is empty?
evals.expected_output: No. The header tab and directly formatted non-breaking-space run are `run_layout` units. Each requires an explicit mapped, default, guidance, unresolved, or not-observable disposition, with local context and any direct-format bindings when mapped/default. The agent may keep an ordinary inherited space under its parent paragraph, but it must not silently discard a tab, break, non-breaking space, or directly formatted whitespace that can affect layout.
expectations: The response distinguishes layout-only runs from ordinary inherited whitespace.
The response requires an explicit atomic disposition for layout-only runs.
The response keeps direct formatting local rather than converting it into a global style rule.

evals.name: empty-word-paragraph-with-layout-is-a-local-evidence-unit
evals.prompt: Between a title and author block, the official Word template has an empty paragraph with explicit `space_after`, centered alignment, and a page-break setting. May the agent drop it because it has no text, or absorb it into global line spacing?
evals.expected_output: No. Extraction records it as a `paragraph.layout` / `paragraph_layout` unit with its exact direct layout evidence and immediate source context. The agent maps it to a local editable blank-paragraph or break helper, or records an explicit gap pending render confirmation. It must not omit the evidence or use it to alter document-wide body leading, margins, or unrelated title spacing.
expectations: The response preserves an empty paragraph when it has explicit layout evidence.
The response treats the result as a local layout boundary with a dedicated editable owner or gap.
The response rejects global spacing adjustments as a substitute for the source boundary.

evals.name: local-layout-units-do-not-merge-across-word-parents
evals.prompt: Two empty Word paragraphs have identical explicit spacing, but one separates the title from the authors and the other separates a figure from body text. A third paragraph contains two directly formatted tab runs. How may the atomic review group these units?
evals.expected_output: The two empty paragraphs must remain separate `paragraph.layout` decisions because they have different Word parent evidence and neighboring semantic blocks, even though their direct formats match. The two tab runs may share one local `run_layout` group only because they belong to the same parent paragraph. The agent must not promote either group into a document-wide spacing or tab rule without stronger repeated source and same-content render evidence.
expectations: The response prohibits cross-parent grouping for paragraph-layout and run-layout evidence.
The response permits bounded grouping only within one Word parent paragraph.
The response preserves local context instead of inferring a global formatting rule.

evals.name: cjk-fixture-anchor-contract-is-language-specific
evals.prompt: A mixed Chinese-English official Word template is normalized with Temp2TeX's CJK latex-default fixture. The generated XeLaTeX PDF and Word-rendered reference have identical A4 page counts, but the PDF comparison says all English stress anchors are missing. May the agent declare the pair not comparable or calibrate from raw pixel difference?
evals.expected_output: No. The agent recognizes this as an invalid English anchor contract, not evidence that the Chinese fixture differs. It writes or requests a language- and profile-specific role-level anchor map, covering the populated bilingual front matter, body/headings, table/caption/note, figure/caption, references, and appendix. It reruns comparison with that map, requires every declared anchor in both PDFs, and only then interprets page flow, image-frame geometry, and visual differences. It must not omit missing Chinese roles merely to pass the contract, and it must preserve any remaining visual mismatch as a format issue rather than treating language selection as a pass.
expectations: The response identifies an English-only anchor map as the source of the false non-comparability result.
The response requires a saved language/profile-specific full-document map before calibration.
The response keeps genuine visual differences open for audit after the text contract passes.

evals.name: fixture-image-frame-contract-precedes-visual-calibration
evals.prompt: A same-content Word-to-LaTeX comparison uses a 4.7-inch raster placeholder in Word but a full-text-width 35 mm framed placeholder in LaTeX. Captions match, yet the PDF diff flags the figures and shifts later content. The image pixels are intentionally irrelevant. Should the agent tune margins, body leading, or float placement to lower the score?
evals.expected_output: No. The agent first records this as a fixture-image-frame contract failure: the two render paths use different width, height, or representation. It aligns the declared figure frame geometry and test-body structure on both sides, then reruns the same-content anchor and visual checks. Raster interiors may be masked only after matching the frame; captions, surrounding whitespace, page flow, and table content remain checked. The agent does not hide the entire figure, use image-content differences to excuse frame mismatch, or tune unrelated class settings before fixture validity is restored.
expectations: The response identifies image-frame geometry as a fixture precondition rather than a journal-class rule.
The response retains caption, surrounding-flow, and table checks while permitting only raster-interior masking.
The response rejects unrelated margin or font tuning until the fixture geometry is aligned.

evals.name: front-matter-metadata-is-typed-not-a-single-style
evals.prompt: An official Word template shows a 9.5 pt DOI line with a bold DOI label, a 9.5 pt classification/article-ID line, and 8 pt received-date, funding, and author-biography lines. They all occur around the title page. May the agent map them through one generic small metadata command because they are all front matter?
evals.expected_output: No. The agent groups only explicit semantic metadata kinds, preserves the line plus label-run and value-run evidence for each kind, and gives each detected kind a separate editable class mapping. It uses `\journalmetadata[kind]{\journalmetadatalabel[kind]{Label:} value}` for a source-backed line and records an untyped metadata command as a documented fallback. It must not use a DOI or funding style as a proxy for another kind, infer metadata from a DOI in body references, or replace evidence with a generic command merely because it compiles.
expectations: The response distinguishes publication identifiers, DOI, dates, funding, contributor notes, and editorial notes as independently evidenced kinds.
The response preserves label and value run formatting rather than treating a full Word line as one font rule.
The response keeps the generic metadata command explicitly default-level and rejects body-reference false positives.

evals.name: typed-metadata-survives-ledger-and-atomic-review
evals.prompt: A Word template has five front-matter metadata paragraphs: classification/article ID, DOI, received dates, funding, and author biography. The title-page visual order is correct, but the format ledger currently calls all five `front_matter.metadata`. Is that sufficient for atomic mapping?
evals.expected_output: No. The ledger must preserve each explicit semantic label as a separate role: `front_matter.metadata.publication_id`, `.doi`, `.dates`, `.funding`, or `.contributor_note` (and `.editorial_note` when present). Each role must carry the exact line, label-run, and value-run evidence plus a typed `\journalmetadata[kind]` class owner. The front-matter sequence review may aggregate the `front_matter.metadata.*` prefix to protect order, but it must not erase the child roles. A DOI inside a body reference must not create a front-matter DOI role.
expectations: The response requires type-specific ledger roles and typed editable ownership.
The response preserves metadata order by aggregating child roles only for sequence review.
The response rejects bibliography/body DOI false positives.

evals.name: typed-metadata-fields-are-exposed-without-copying-article-data
evals.prompt: The official Word template visibly contains a DOI label, classification code, funding line, received dates, and author biography. The generated class has typed metadata macros, but `main.tex` only contains an empty generic metadata call. Is that an adequate editable template handoff?
evals.expected_output: No. The package must expose a commented `metadata.tex` field skeleton and a commented input line in `main.tex`. The skeleton provides a source-backed typed command and label for each observed kind, such as `\journalmetadata[doi]{\journalmetadatalabel[doi]{DOI:} ...}`, but omits article-specific values such as an actual DOI, grant number, received date, or biography. The model must not hide all fields behind one empty generic command or copy sample manuscript data into the default template.
expectations: The response requires a visible but inactive editable field skeleton for every observed metadata type.
The response keeps source labels and omits source article values.
The response rejects an empty generic metadata call as the only user-facing interface.

evals.name: english-font-engine-contract-is-explicit-and-portable
evals.prompt: An English-only official Word template uses Times New Roman. The generated class loads `fontspec` so the source font renders under XeLaTeX, but the package README does not name an engine and a user runs PDFLaTeX. What must the agent provide?
evals.expected_output: The agent must make the engine contract explicit. XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX may use a source-backed system font after availability checks; an English-only package may additionally support PDFLaTeX through a documented TeX font fallback. It must not load `fontspec` unconditionally, let PDFLaTeX fail without guidance, or weaken Chinese/mixed-language packages into PDFLaTeX compatibility. Chinese and mixed-language output remains explicitly XeLaTeX-only.
expectations: The response states a visible compile-engine contract in the generated package README.
The response requires a conditional font branch rather than unconditional fontspec in English-only output.
The response preserves XeLaTeX as a hard requirement for Chinese or mixed-language output.

evals.name: missing-abstract-limit-keeps-the-template-language-default
evals.prompt: A Chinese-first Word journal template contains no official abstract length rule. The generated `format_gap_log.md` says `English default: concise abstract without hard word limit`. Is this acceptable because no numeric limit was invented?
evals.expected_output: No. The agent may leave the limit unset, but the logged default must match the inferred template language. A `zh` template records a concise Chinese-abstract default, a `mixed` template records a source-language abstract-block default, and an `en` template records the English default. The agent must not impose a numeric word count, describe a Chinese template with an English fallback, or label a documented default as an official rule.
expectations: The response preserves an unset abstract limit when official evidence is absent.
The response requires language-consistent default wording in the gap log.
The response distinguishes an explicit default from a source-backed rule.

evals.name: spec-output-path-is-an-isolated-workspace-contract
evals.prompt: An agent inspects an official Word template and writes `template_spec.json` to a new per-journal output directory. The directory does not yet exist. May the spec-extraction command assume the agent created it manually?
evals.expected_output: No. The spec-extraction tool must create the parent directory for an explicit output path, so an isolated per-journal workflow does not fail before evidence review starts. The agent still records the source inventory and must not treat successful file creation as proof that any format role is mapped or verified.
expectations: The response requires automatic parent-directory creation for the explicit spec output path.
The response preserves isolated per-journal workspaces.
The response does not equate successful extraction with formatting fidelity.

evals.name: abstract-limit-preserves-language-unit-and-conflict
evals.prompt: Official guidance says `中文摘要不超过300字`; another template says `Abstract must not exceed 250 words`; a third source gives conflicting limits of 200 and 250 words. How should the agent write `template_spec.json` and the gap log?
evals.expected_output: The agent records each unambiguous limit with its original unit and source excerpt: 300 `characters` for the Chinese rule and 250 `words` for the English rule. It does not convert characters to words or infer a length rule from an ordinary abstract sample. For conflicting official limits, it preserves the candidates, leaves the limit unset, and records an ambiguity in `format_gap_log.md`; it must not select one value merely because it is common.
expectations: The response keeps `words` and Chinese `characters` as distinct source units.
The response requires an explicit abstract limit cue rather than a nearby number.
The response leaves conflicting source limits unresolved and auditable.

evals.name: keyword-count-is-explicit-language-aware-and-auditable
evals.prompt: Official guidance says `Keywords: 3 to 6`; a Chinese template says `关键词不超过5个`; another Word sample merely shows four keywords; a conflicting guide says 4 to 6. What count constraint belongs in the generated spec?
evals.expected_output: The agent records the first source rule as minimum 3 and maximum 6, and the Chinese rule as maximum 5, each with source evidence. It does not infer a four-keyword maximum from a sample list. When official constraints conflict, it keeps the candidates, leaves the count unset, and logs the ambiguity. If no count is observable, it records a language-matched concise-list default rather than inventing a limit.
expectations: The response requires an explicit keyword constraint and preserves range bounds.
The response rejects sample-keyword counting as a source rule.
The response keeps conflicts and absent limits auditable rather than guessing.

evals.name: fresh-workspace-output-and-legacy-word-provenance
evals.prompt: An agent inspects an official legacy `.doc` template into a previously absent per-journal directory. The helper fails because `source_inventory.json`'s parent directory does not exist. May the agent write the inventory elsewhere or treat a LibreOffice DOCX as the official source?
evals.expected_output: No. The inspection helper must create the explicit output parent so every journal can use an isolated workspace. It may convert the legacy file to a temporary DOCX for structural inspection, but the original DOC remains the official evidence and the inventory must record the conversion provenance. Successful temporary conversion does not establish final layout fidelity.
expectations: The response requires automatic parent-directory creation for explicit outputs.
The response preserves original legacy Word authority and conversion provenance.
The response does not equate successful conversion with a fidelity pass.

evals.name: word-ledger-package-exposes-required-atomic-next-step
evals.prompt: A generated LaTeX package contains copied `word_format_ledger.json`, but no atomic decisions or system triage have been completed. Its README merely says `review unresolved entries`. May the agent present this as a completed ordinary conversion?
evals.expected_output: No. The README must state that inspectable Word evidence does not establish fidelity, and provide the concrete next commands to create the pending atomic-decision starter, initialize system-format triage, and prepare a bounded review batch. The agent must keep unresolved items open, merge only evidence-bound final decisions, and rerun the atomic audit before ordinary-delivery claims. Compilation or a plausible PDF cannot replace this review.
expectations: The response distinguishes generated package files from completed atomic mapping.
The response requires an executable starter, system-triage, and bounded-review workflow.
The response rejects compilation or visual plausibility as a replacement for source-unit decisions.

evals.name: default-only-floats-cannot-authorize-full-class-calibration
evals.prompt: A sparse official Word template has no observable table and no inline body figure. A normalizer injects a sample table and raster placeholder into Word, while the generated LaTeX package uses the same neutral bitmap for PDF comparison. Every text anchor occurs in both PDFs, but table notes and later content paginate differently. May the agent call this a full-document comparison and tune global margins, leading, or float rules?
evals.expected_output: No. The injected objects can exercise the package interfaces and the shared bitmap can verify image frame geometry while masking only its raster interior. However, the source did not establish table or body-artwork structure, so the anchor map must be `partial_zone` (or the pair must otherwise be marked unsuitable for whole-class calibration), with the limitation recorded. The agent may inspect the local diagnostic but must not use its table, image, page-flow, or body-density differences to alter global class rules. A full-document contract requires source-observable or independently verified shared structure for every populated table and figure.
expectations: The response distinguishes source-observable objects from injected fixture coverage.
The response permits a shared raster placeholder only for frame-aware, image-interior-insensitive diagnostics.
The response blocks global class calibration from default-only table or figure flow.

evals.name: anchored-word-artwork-counts-as-object-evidence
evals.prompt: An official Word template has two real tables and a body figure stored as a DrawingML `wp:anchor`. A basic Word library reports zero `inline_shapes`, so a comparison helper labels the source as having no body artwork and downgrades it to a default-only partial fixture. Is that an acceptable readiness decision?

It may still need a same-content shared representation before a full PDF calibration, but it must not be treated as absent simply because a convenience library exposes only inline shapes. Non-image text boxes or decorative rules alone do not establish generic figure-fixture evidence.
expectations: The response counts image-bearing anchored DrawingML objects as source evidence.
The response keeps anchored-image geometry and caption relation distinct from generic text boxes or rules.
The response preserves the separate same-content fixture requirement before full visual calibration.

evals.name: grid-table-preamble-is-resolved-before-regression-compilation
evals.prompt: A Word table has three source-backed columns and a full grid. The generated class exposes `\journaltablerepresentativecolspec`, whose definition contains `@{}` material and vertical rules. The package must then compile with the grid rules and proportional widths still present; do not replace the source grid with a generic `lll` table just to make the test compile.
expectations: The response identifies the tabular preamble expansion boundary rather than blaming the TeX engine.
The response retains source-backed grid borders and relative widths in the compiled stress fixture.
The response requires a fresh compile and rejects any partial PDF emitted before the fatal error.

evals.name: english-regression-shares-single-and-paired-image-frames
evals.prompt: The English Word stress normalizer inserts one single-panel and one paired-panel raster placeholder. The agent must not hide unmatched figure regions or promote a float/margin change from that invalid fixture.
expectations: The response uses separate matching single- and paired-panel comparison assets.
The response preserves empty editable frames for ordinary delivery.
The response rejects whole-zone image masking and unrelated layout tuning.

evals.name: system-triage-priority-orders-work-without-closing-evidence
evals.prompt: A Word ledger produces 400 pending system-format children. The producer-order first page consists largely of long template instructions with minor character spacing, while later source-backed cards include an equation tab stop, a table cell, and a heading. What review batch should the agent request, what must each card expose, and may priority silently mark instruction cards as guidance?
evals.expected_output: The agent requests a bounded pending-only `prepare_system_format_triage.py` batch with `--review-order priority`. It may use `--review-order source-order` for a forensic recheck. Priority is not a disposition: every child remains pending until an evidence-bound final decision is written and strict audit is rerun.
expectations: The response distinguishes a deterministic review order from a child disposition or audit pass.
The response keeps all system children and exposes an alternative forensic source-order pass.
The response requires source locator, observed value, linked ordinary evidence, rank, and rank reason on review cards.

evals.name: reopened-triage-refreshes-pending-links-but-rejects-final-link-mutation
evals.prompt: A prior system-triage queue linked a table-cell theme sample to body paragraph `p0001` because the Word object used a table-local paragraph index that collided with the document index. For the finalized child, it must stop and require explicit rebuild/review; it must not silently alter the source link or preserve a conclusion under different evidence. Matching the ledger fingerprint alone does not authorize mutation of finalized provenance.
expectations: The response refreshes only pending producer-owned source fields.
The response rejects a changed source link on a final child rather than silently migrating it.

evals.name: system-queue-initialization-precedes-but-does-not-block-ordinary-role-mapping

It alternates ordinary batches with priority-ordered linked system-child reviews, uses reconciliation only after the relevant ordinary decisions are final, and runs strict atomic audit only after both ordinary units and every required system child have final evidence-bound dispositions.
expectations: The response distinguishes queue creation from finalizing all system children.
The response allows only readiness-selected ordinary mapping after a matching queue exists.
The response keeps the full strict audit blocked until both ordinary and system decisions are final.

evals.name: tool-unavailable-conversion-keeps-manual-unit-ledger-and-audit

The response preserves source/default/gap status and an owner or pending check for every unit.
The response delivers an editable package without claiming unavailable compile or visual verification.

evals.name: deterministic-regression-baseline-is-not-an-llm-skill-result
evals.prompt: A 60-case `run_regression.py` report says `executor_model: local-regression-runner`, `tokens: 0`, and several packages compiled. Its benchmark configuration is labelled `with_skill`. evals.name: compiled-draft-cannot-bypass-package-validation-gate

evals.name: active-suppress-overlap-remains-an-evidence-bound-gap
evals.prompt: An official RSC Word template scan finds two unmodeled OOXML properties: w:noProof on several runs, and w:suppressOverlap on a paragraph with no documented value or publisher explanation. The response retains source locator, attributes, and role context for suppressOverlap.

evals.name: stale-package-validation-report-cannot-authorize-handoff

evals.name: cjk-engine-contract-rejects-pdflatex-declaration

evals.name: word-asset-manifest-binds-media-to-deliverable-files

evals.name: reference-fixture-requires-citation-entry-and-editable-bib

evals.name: main-fixture-must-exercise-core-template-modules
evals.prompt: A package supplies a detailed journal-template.cls with custom title, abstract, table, figure, equation, and footnote interfaces, but main.tex contains only a title, two body paragraphs, and comments showing the other commands. Add neutral placeholders through the class interfaces, then compile the final package.

The response distinguishes active class ownership from manually duplicated article settings.

evals.name: handoff-status-distinguishes-checkpoint-from-completion
evals.prompt: The agent has generated a compilable LaTeX package from an official Word template, but 40 source-backed paragraph and table decisions remain in the atomic audit. What provenance must be retained before ordinary delivery?
evals.expected_output: The original .doc remains authoritative. evals.name: handoff-ready-state-must-match-current-package-fingerprint

The PDF still compiles. May it be delivered as an ordinary completed conversion?

Run validation again to confirm the final handoff state. The status file itself may be updated without changing the fingerprint, but any substantive package input change requires this cycle.
expectations: The response rejects a ready handoff whose package fingerprint predates a substantive package edit.
The response distinguishes the final status-file update from an editable package change.
The response requires a fresh validation and a second validation after the ready-state update.

evals.name: readiness-and-validator-share-handoff-fingerprint-contract
evals.prompt: A completed Temp2TeX package has a valid package_validation.json and HANDOFF_STATUS.md records `Ordinary handoff: ready`, `Package validation: valid`, and the validator's current fingerprint. expectations: The response identifies conflicting fingerprint implementations rather than treating a valid report as stale by default.
The response excludes HANDOFF_STATUS.md from both fingerprints but continues to require and validate it.
The response preserves stale detection for substantive editable-package changes.

evals.name: tool-unavailable-delivery-is-not-a-mapping-checkpoint
evals.prompt: An agent has completed Word source capture, strict atomic mapping, ownership checks, and an editable class-based package. A normal `ready` state is invalid without an available environment, valid package validation, and the current fingerprint.
expectations: The response distinguishes unavailable local verification from incomplete source mapping.
The response gives the exact paired handoff, validation, fingerprint, and environment states.

evals.name: front-matter-style-candidates-force-sequence-confirmation

Because these are candidates rather than final source classifications, front_matter_sequence_review must mark semantic confirmation as required and list the ordered evidence IDs. The agent resolves title, author, affiliation, and metadata from visible context before promoting class interfaces; it must not silently map the author to title or the affiliation to a heading.
expectations: The response preserves title, author, and affiliation candidates with their Word evidence rather than silently discarding or flattening them.
The response requires a blocking front-matter sequence confirmation for candidate-only roles.
The response does not promote a Word style name alone into an unreviewed final class rule.

evals.name: front-matter-confirmation-is-ledger-bound-and-progresses-the-loop
evals.prompt: A Word ledger has a blocking front_matter_sequence_review for three candidate records: p0001 title, p0002 author, and p0003 affiliation. What artifact and validation sequence must Temp2TeX require?
evals.expected_output: Create front_matter_semantic_confirmation.json from the ledger-bound starter. It must retain the ledger fingerprint and confirm each exact evidence ID, source index, and candidate role once, with a visible-context reason. Rerun conversion readiness; it may proceed only after the confirmation validates. Rerunning the unchanged ledger alone does not resolve the gate. If the Word context contradicts a candidate, keep the issue open as an evidence gap rather than silently substituting another role. Package validation must reject a missing, stale, pending, duplicate, or role-mutating confirmation file.
expectations: The response creates a fingerprint-bound confirmation artifact with one complete record per ordered front-matter candidate.
The response uses readiness to advance only after a valid confirmation, avoiding an unchanged-ledger loop.
The response preserves unresolved evidence disagreements instead of silently relabelling source roles.

evals.name: front-matter-style-does-not-overrule-explicit-author-instruction
evals.prompt: A Word template has a `Title` style paragraph reading `A General Journal Template`, an `Author List` style paragraph reading `List all authors in a comma-delimited list`, an `Affiliation` style paragraph reading `Present author addresses below the names`, and a starred line `* Correspondence: name@example.org`. How must Temp2TeX classify these records?
evals.expected_output: Keep the non-imperative title-style sample as a front_matter.title candidate, even though it includes the word Template. Keep the two imperative authoring sentences as guidance.instruction evidence despite their Author List and Affiliation styles. Classify the starred Correspondence line as typed front_matter.metadata.contributor_note. The resulting front-matter sequence review may require confirmation for the true title candidate, while the instruction lines must not become author or affiliation interfaces.
expectations: The response preserves a non-imperative title-style sample as a candidate.
The response classifies explicit authoring directives as guidance despite their named Word styles.
The response classifies a starred Correspondence line as typed contributor metadata.
